tasks.title: Separate definition, executor and target identities
tasks.goal: Freeze the environment roles and compatibility interpretation before existing host-based consumers acquire new fields.
steps: First create/update the governing permanent anchors in vibevm/vibespecs/common/PROP-063-environment-model.xml for this task's contract, with desired-versus-implemented status explicit. Only then add executable types or tests citing those anchors. Final promotion/retirement records evidence later; it is not permission to postpone the source contract.
Trace each existing host/OS/platform field to its current meaning; list old-reader behavior and exact callers requiring an explicit target later.

Define EnvironmentDefinition, EnvironmentLock, ExecutionContext, TargetBinding and EnvironmentGeneration as separate identities; distinguish build machine, produced-tool runtime and compiler output target.
Add pure type constructors and compatibility results for workspace, HOME, offline rootfs and future live targets; preserve existing bare-install behavior and reject unimplemented targets explicitly.
positive_cases: Existing project install binds to an explicit local target with unchanged semantics.
A Windows executor can describe a Linux target without selecting a Windows launcher.
negative_cases: Executor ABI is substituted for target ABI.
Future live-system capability is advertised as implemented.
checks: SELECT BEFORE DISPATCH: vibe-core target/cases are TO BIND from source/metadata to affected positive/negative obligations; choose --lib, --test <name>, --bin <name>, or affected --doc before compiling.

RUN BOUND CHECKS: after binding, use cargo test -p vibe-core <target> <case> -- --exact for lib/test/bin, or a reviewed small family without --exact; bind supported rustdoc selection separately. Verify intended nonzero cases in output; use target-specific --list only when needed to confirm selection, and reuse its valid inventory.
TO CREATE: environment-role and legacy-host-guard contract tests in vibe-core.
acceptance: Each identity has named inputs and owned authority; no environment becomes a new package kind or stewardship DB.
Pure construction needs neither Docker nor a host HOME lookup.
tasks.safe_stop: Types and compatibility tests are coherent; downstream consumers remain on their explicit legacy interpretation.

tasks.title: Centralize environment layout and prefix policy
tasks.goal: Provide one injected layout/root policy for user profiles and offline targets without scattering machine paths through providers.
steps: Locate the existing layout authority named by the baseline and enumerate environment configuration, store, profile, state and cache roots.
Implement pure root-relative resource identity with environment instance, principal, path/case policy and prefix compatibility; preserve the existing project vibevm/ layout.
Represent relocatable, prefix-bound and unsupported payload compatibility and reserved future account/service/mount/boot resources; inject selected roots instead of re-reading ambient HOME/PATH.
positive_cases: Two definitions can share immutable content yet have different target instance/root authority.
Valid Linux payload components survive Windows control-plane validation.
negative_cases: A reused pathname silently transfers an old receipt to a different root.
